**Finding: missing (insurance provision absent) — redline validated and submitted.**

Summary of the work:

- **Investigation:** A document-wide search for "insurance" returned zero hits, and the section outline confirmed there is no insurance heading. The miscellaneous provisions (Sections 13–30, all housed in `sec-12`) cover assignment, notices, governing law, force majeure, etc., but nothing on coverage.
- **Direction check:** The obligation runs against TrueLink, the counterparty. TrueLink hosts our Web Site and processes Client Content plus consumer credit data under the System and Credit Repository Agreements, so it squarely fits the "vendor that touches our data" trigger. This is a burden on them and a benefit to us, so flagging is appropriate.
- **Why it matters here:** TrueLink's indemnity (Section 12.b) and the liability cap in Section 12 (12 months of hosting/support fees for Sections 3, 4, 7 and 11 claims) exist with no insurance backstop at all — a data-breach or E&O loss would have no funded source of recovery.

**Redline (preferred position):**
1. New **Section 31 (INSURANCE)** inserted after Section 30, requiring CGL of USD 1M per occurrence / 2M aggregate, E&O of USD 2M, cyber/privacy of USD 5M, statutory workers' compensation, maintained through the term plus one year, with certificates on request.
2. One conforming tweak to **Section 24**: survival list changed from "Sections 1 and 5 through 30" to "5 through 31," so the one-year post-term coverage obligation actually survives termination. Without this the new clause would fall outside the survival range and the tail coverage would be unenforceable after expiry.

The comment flags the fallback (E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M) as available if TrueLink pushes back on limits.
